sentences.text: I note that the UEC scheme ended on December 2025, and I ask that an extension be considered.

sections.label: SNEF reservations and tripartite workgroup
sections.summary: SNEF's CEO wrote of strong reservations; a Tripartite Workgroup reviews the Employment Act, and NTUC's standpoint was shared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Shortly thereafter, the chief executive officer (CEO) of SNEF wrote to The Straits Times to share that, I think the words were: "they have strong reservations about this call." Can I ask the Member, in view of the tripartite framework, has there been agreement with SNEF on this particular point?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: On the Member's question, there are tripartite negotiations on this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: We have formed a Tripartite Workgroup on the review of the Employment Act which I am a member, we are looking at this carefully to balance the interests of the respective tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: But what I shared earlier is our NTUC's standpoint, which both Secretary-General and myself have shared earlier.

sections.label: HDB blocks ageing and Budget surplus
sections.summary: More HDB blocks are crossing 50 years, while a 2025 Budget surplus over $15 billion will be added to reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But more and more of our HDB blocks are also crossing the 50-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is good news indeed that we had managed to achieve a Budget surplus of over $15 billion for 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The surplus will be added to our reserves, where we can generate investment income streams that will contribute to our future Budgets.

sections.label: Additional round of HDB HIP
sections.summary: As HIP runs only twice in 99 years, HDB is asked to review its policy and consider an extra, more flexible HIP round.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As the HDB Home Improvement Programme (HIP) takes place only twice during the span of the 99 years, residents are left waiting and are appealing for a more lasting and sustained solution to the myriad of problems affecting their blocks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To deal with the systemic deterioration of such HDB blocks, could the HDB review its HIP policy and consider an additional round of HIP which is more flexible in scope to take into account the specific issues faced by a particular HDB estate?

sections.label: Sky garden disamenities and enforcement measures
sections.summary: Disamenities persist despite efforts by volunteers, HDB, Town Council, NEA and police; MND is asked to reconsider gantries, CCTVs, visitor limits and fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These problems have not abated, even with the concerted efforts of our grassroots volunteers, the HDB, Town Council, the National Environment Agency (NEA) and the police, disamenities still persist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I appeal to MND once again, to reconsider my previous suggestions: install gantries for registration, install more closed circuit televisions (CCTVs) to monitor visitors and their activities, limit the number of visitors and require payment of a small fee to support the operations and cleaning of the sky gardens.

sections.label: Property tax rebate for retirees
sections.summary: Former earners face higher property taxes paid from savings, and the Government is asked to consider a longer-term rebate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The anxiety is real, especially as they are no longer earning an income and yet face increasingly higher property taxes that they are paying for out of their own savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider granting a longer-term rebate for such cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My concern, however, is that the take-up rate for such initiatives will not be as high as desired, given what we have seen with the SkillsFuture credits where many people left it to the final months, and even then, it was not fully taken up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA’s) SG Digital Community Hubs be expanded to help seniors and more Singaporeans gain AI skills and pick up safety tips?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned about the potential low take-up as with SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to make AI resources more easily accessible, expand SG Digital Community Hubs to help seniors and providing stronger career guidance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: MOF's Occasional Paper on Medium-Term Fiscal Projections in 2023 sends a very clear signal – our total spending will go up to around 19.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030, driven by healthcare for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 is a milestone in the sense that it is the first Budget since the Occasional Paper to hit that 19.5% of GDP in total revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: With the increase in headline GST rate from 7% to 9%, GST collection has gone up from around 2% of GDP to 2.6% in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Long-term corporate tax assumption
sections.summary: It argues against relying on BEPS and suggests revising the long-term corporate income tax assumption to 4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Indeed, a real failure of long-term fiscal marksmanship will be if we bet on something as new and uncertain as BEPS for our long-term fiscal future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, taken together, we can probably revise our long-term assumption for corporate income tax revenues upwards to 4% of GDP, not 4.5% as in Budget 2026, but 4%.

sections.label: Raising property tax collections
sections.summary: It notes early 2000s property tax collections of 1% to 1.1% of GDP and proposes raising them to 1.2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But not too long ago, in the early 2000s, property tax collections were as high as 1% to 1.1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I think we should aim to raise property tax collections to 1.2% of GDP in the long term and focus on the top tier of residential properties.

sections.label: Surpluses and pandemic deficit
sections.summary: It cites FY2016 to FY2019 surpluses and a $51.6 billion deficit, 10.8% of GDP, to fight the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: In FYs 2016 to 2019, we had a pretty good run – Budget surpluses of 1.4%, 2.3% and 0.7% of GDP, successively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: A deficit of $51.6 billion, 10.8% of GDP, to fight the crisis of a generation.

sections.label: Assessing recent fiscal surpluses
sections.summary: It compares FY2000, FY2025 and FY2026 surpluses and calls the recent ones modest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And further back, in FY2000, we had a surplus of 2.4% of GDP, although it was just $4 billion in dollar terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And so, in my view, the surplus for FY2025 at 1.9% of GDP is somewhat modest, hardly the greatest fiscal surplus any PAP Government has seen in decades; and the surplus for FY2026 at 1% of GDP is decidedly modest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The accumulated surplus over the last term of Government, including the surplus for FY2025, is at around 0.6% of cumulative GDP, again, decidedly modest in my view.

sections.label: Extending GST offsets
sections.summary: It proposes ploughing back part of the surpluses to extend transitional GST offsets by one more year for most Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Plough back part of the surpluses to extend our transitional GST offsets by one more year for the vast majority of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Balance of spending and saving
sections.summary: It says balance concerns societal spending and saving, and describes combining two versions of a quote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: My idea of balance that I prompted you on was not so much about keeping versus sharing at the individual level, but about spending and saving at the societal level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Take only what is needed, leave the rest as sustenance for God's nature".

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But I really liked the second line from the first version, so responding to the Minister of State Jasmin Lau's exhortation yesterday, I exercised my human agency and critical thinking, and I combined the two versions.

sections.label: FY2021 surplus and FY2023 deficit
sections.summary: FY2021 had a surplus of 0.3% of GDP and FY2023 a deficit of 0.4% of GDP, taken as largely balanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: The surplus that we had for FY2021 was just 0.3% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In FY2023, we had a deficit of 0.4% of GDP – and I took those to be largely balanced.

sections.label: MOF paper and GST revenue
sections.summary: A 2023 MOF paper states total spending needs will reach 19% to 20% of GDP by 2030, and GST yields 0.6% of GDP more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: For the first, I would say, let us go back to the MOF Occasional Paper published in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And it is stated very clearly in that paper that our total spending needs will hit 19% to 20% of GDP by 2030; the midpoint is 19.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: If the Member had listened to my speech and looked at the data, GST even with the increase from 7% to 9% headline rate, is yielding 0.6% of GDP more revenues – from 2% to 2.6% in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: GST alone hardly covers us up to the 19.5% target.

sections.label: 6.9 million population planning parameter
sections.summary: The ruling party uses 6.9 million as a population planning parameter and should explain the limit in the population plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the ruling party uses 6.9 million as a population planning parameter, they should at least give Singaporeans an explanation – what exactly is the limit in the population plan?

sections.label: 6.9 million planning parameter and infrastructure
sections.summary: Government said 6.9 million remains a relevant planning parameter for the 2030s, with population size depending on trends and needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government last month said in response to Aljunied MP Fadli Fawzi's question that, while the oft quoted number of 6.9 million is still a relevant planning parameter for the 2030s, our population size, not limits, depend on demographic trends and social and economic needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If 6.9 million is just a planning parameter, then the question Singaporeans living in high density communities like Sengkang need to see answered is this: at that parameter, what precisely does our infrastructure plan to provide and at what point does this provision start to cause discomfort?

sections.label: Regional population projections proposal
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government would consider releasing population projections for each region under URA plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To relieve concerns, would the Government consider releasing population projections for each region as part of the Urban Redevelopment Authority's plans?

sections.label: Population, dependency ratio and care work
sections.summary: Population and demographics are intertwined with the rising dependency ratio, a megatrend, and its implications for care work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Next, population and demographics are intertwined with our rising dependency ratio, megatrend and its implications for care work.

sections.label: Beijing vehicle licence plate lottery births
sections.summary: A 2018 Journal of Development Economics study found Beijing's vehicle licence plate lottery was associated with a 35% reduction in births in participants' households and 6% citywide.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, research published in the Journal of Development Economics in 2018 found that the Beijing vehicle licence plate lottery system was associated with a 35% reduction in births in households of lottery participants and a 6% reduction in births across the entire city.

sections.label: Domestic worker rest day and HSS
sections.summary: A 2021 rule requires employers to give domestic workers one non-compensable rest day monthly, and the passage asks whether this is enough and about HSS awareness.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2021, a rule was introduced, requiring employers to provide domestic workers at least one rest day a month that cannot be compensated away.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Has the Government more recently assessed if it is enough?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With basic childminding services no longer being supported with manpower concessions under the HSS pilot from next month, is the Government working with providers to raise awareness of more general HSS services under the scheme?

sections.label: Ban on in-person play concerns
sections.summary: The passage cites concerns about in-person play, the Flynn effect, and other countries' laws, and calls for a Select Committee to study whether a ban is appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is concerning as in-person play develops critical social and coping skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There has also been increasing concern about the plateauing of or even reversal of the Flynn effect, which states that younger generations score higher on IQ test compared with the previous ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Australia's laws came into effect in December last year, with countries like Spain, India, Denmark, Norway, Malaysia and the UK announcing similar intentions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is time for Singapore to take clearer scientifically informed interventions to address these concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This should include setting up a Select Committee to study whether a ban is appropriate in par in parallel to the Government's ongoing study and engagement with counterparts.

sections.label: National AI Council societal representation
sections.summary: The new National AI Council must include representatives from societal sectors at high risk of adverse AI effects, not only industrial AI Missions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, at the top level, the new National AI Council must include representatives from the societal sectors that are at high risk for adverse effects from AI, rather than only boosting adoption via industrial AI Missions.

sections.label: MIT study on AI overreliance
sections.summary: A study last year by MIT Media Lab found overreliance on AI may reduce functional brain connectivity and memory recall, despite MOE frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While various MOE frameworks are in place, a study last year by MIT Media Lab found that over reliance on AI may reduce functional brain connectivity and memory recall.

sections.label: Legal boundaries for protected nature areas
sections.summary: As called for in a 2024 Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan, the Government should set clear legal boundaries for protected nature areas and protect remaining habitats.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As called for in a 2024 Singapore Terrestrial Conservation Plan, the Government should establish clear legal boundaries for protected nature areas and protect the few remaining habitats that we have, which are absolutely key for both planetary and societal health.

sections.label: Southeast Asia per capita income
sections.summary: Singapore ranks second in Southeast Asia at about US$22,000 per capita, behind Brunei and ahead of Malaysia, Thailand and the regional average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In Southeast Asia, on a per capita basis, we are number two in 2024, at about US$22,000 per capita, behind Brunei.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We are ahead of Malaysia which is about US$10,000; Thailand, about US$5,500; and the Southeast Asia average of about US$3,500 and we are close to the OECD average of about US$23,000.

sections.label: Singapore OECD spending comparison
sections.summary: Within the OECD, Singapore's per capita spending is just behind the US and UK and ahead of Korea and Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Within the OECD, Singapore is just behind the spending of US, which is about US$26,000; and the UK, which is about US$24,000; and ahead of Korea and Japan, both at about US$19,000.

sections.label: Retraining, fitness, CPF rates
sections.summary: The Government must keep people fit to work, skilled and growing retirement savings through three measures including compulsory retraining and higher CPF rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Government must keep our people fit to work, acquire relevant skills and grow their retirement nest egg.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: So, we need to do three things: one, compulsory retraining and skill upgrade every 10 years; two, staying physically and mentally fit to work; and three, increase forced savings rate or CPF contribution rates.

sections.label: MOM MTI MOE collaboration
sections.summary: MOM, MTI and MOE must collaborate to close gaps between industry needs, job projections and retraining courses, with funding considered for workers at 40, 50 and 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: MOM, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and MOE must collaborate more closely to close the gap between industry needs in high-growth sectors, jobs projections and retraining or re-education courses, for example in sustainability, healthcare and information technology (IT).

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I ask for the Government to consider funding workers for retraining or reskilling for every worker reaching 40, 50 and 60 for six months.

sections.label: Low income retirement sum shortfall
sections.summary: Many low- and lower-middle income groups cannot meet the minimum retirement sum, which must keep increasing, and may lack savings or need to downgrade flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Many low- and lower-middle income groups cannot even meet the minimum retirement sum and yet we know that it has to keep increasing so as to keep pace with inflation and longer life spans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Many in these groups also do not have savings and may have to downgrade their flats or opt for Lease Buybacks.

sections.label: Retirement Account funds for BTO
sections.summary: After appeals, special approval let them use limited Retirement Account funds for their BTO, but they pledged their flat to CPF Board as funds were below the Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: After many rounds of appeals, they finally received special approval to use their limited funds in the Retirement Account for their BTO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: But they had to pledge their flat to CPF Board because the funds in their Retirement Account were below the Basic Retirement Sum.

sections.label: CPF contribution rate consideration
sections.summary: Higher CPF contribution rates from employer and employees may need consideration with more Ordinary Account funds used for property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, with more use of the funds in the Ordinary Account for property purchases, we may need to consider higher CPF contribution rate from employer and employees.

sections.label: Retraining and employability
sections.summary: The passage advocates institutionalising retraining, aligning education with market demands, and viewing work as lifelong and health as an asset.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Every employee is an important link in the chain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: We should seriously consider institutionalising retraining arrangement, for example, allowing an employee to undergo training every 10 years, promoting closer alignment between the education system and market demands with appropriate Government subsidies to establish a more comprehensive retraining system, thereby maintaining employees' employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I also encourage Singaporeans to view work as a lifelong meaningful endeavour rather than merely as a means to retire early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I also advocate for continuous skills upgrading and regarding health as a key asset, so as to ensure our employability and competitiveness in the long term. : Mr Speaker, there is great urgency and courage required of us to carry out this revamp.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Urgency because otherwise, the young seniors will become a "lost generation", which the Singapore Government will need to support for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: No amount of CDC vouchers and subsidies would help us tackle this problem.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger
sections.summary: SSG and WSG will merge into one agency overseen by MOM and MOE to tighten training and jobs links.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SSG and WSG will merge into a single agency, jointly overseen by MOM and MOE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will tighten the link between training and jobs, offering more seamless career guidance, upskilling, job matching and transitions for workers and integrated support for employers.

sections.label: SSG training participation 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, 606,000 individuals participated in SSG-supported training and 123,000 enrolled in courses with direct employability outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, 606,000 individuals participated in SSG-supported training, and 123,000 enrolled in courses with direct employability outcomes.

sections.label: Retrenchments rose in 2025
sections.summary: Retrenchments rose to 14,400 in 2025 amid a choppy global outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Retrenchments rose to 14,400 in 2025, on the back of a choppy global outlook.

sections.label: Permanent and fixed term employment
sections.summary: Over 90% of resident employees are in permanent jobs, around 7% on fixed term contracts, with older workers disproportionately on one-year contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the share declined slightly in 2025, with over 90% of resident employees now in permanent jobs, around 7% remain on fixed term contracts and older workers are disproportionately represented among one-year contracts.

sections.label: CPF increases and investment pilot
sections.summary: CPF contribution increases for senior workers proceed from January 2027 with a transition offset, and a simplified investment scheme is piloted by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next step of planned CPF contribution increases for senior workers will proceed from January 2027, with a transition offset to help employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CPF will also pilot a new simplified, low cost, life-cycle investment scheme by 2028 to give members more diversified options above the base interest rates.

sections.label: Training leave and Public Service norms
sections.summary: Negotiated training leave must spread to non-union and SME settings, and the Public Service can catalyse norms through dashboards and clearer pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where unions are present, we have negotiated training leave into collective agreements; this must be spread by example into non-union and SME settings, with redesigned shifts, modular stackable courses and just-in-time learning aligned to job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Public Service can catalyse norms through transparent dashboards on contract renewal patterns and clearer pathways from fixed term contracts to permanent posts when work is ongoing.

sections.label: Budget 2026 household support
sections.summary: Families will still feel Budget 2026's support: cash Cost-of-Living Special Payments, enhanced U-Save rebates and CDC vouchers in January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Families will still feel Budget 2026's tangible support: cash Cost-of-Living Special Payments, enhanced U-Save rebates and CDC vouchers for all households in January 2027.

sections.label: 3Cs for 2026 Budget debate
sections.summary: The speaker will contribute "3Cs" to the 2026 Budget debate: Cost of living, Caring for families, and Core of our Workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Today, I will contribute "3Cs" to our 2026 Budget debate – Cost of living; Caring for families; and Core of our Workforce.

sections.label: Question on healthy surplus
sections.summary: Some sought clarification on why a healthy surplus of 1.9% of GDP has not already translated to more support measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Some sought clarification – why a healthy surplus to the tune of 1.9% of GDP has not already translated to more support measures.

sections.label: Reviewing revenue measures and taxes
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government would consider re-timing or reviewing planned revenue generating measures or taxes in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: My question is, would the Government consider re-timing or reviewing planned revenue generating measures or taxes in the next few years, especially ones which may directly lead to alleviating cost-of-living pressures?

sections.label: Wage growth and cost pressures
sections.summary: The speaker says broad-based wage growth outpacing inflation is the most sustainable way to help Singaporeans cope with cost pressures, and suggests future Cost-of-Living Special Payments be tiered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: And that in the longer term, the most sustainable way to help Singaporeans cope with cost pressures is through broad-based wage growth that outpaces inflation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: This reminds me of the Chinese saying, "授人以鱼, 不如授人以渔", similar to the English saying: "Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime." While I am aligned with the wisdom behind the design and appreciate the new Cost-of-Living Special Payment, perhaps future iterations can have a tiered structure for a range of income with larger payouts concentrated at the lower spectrum of the income range.

sections.label: Preschool subsidy income threshold
sections.summary: Raising the monthly household income threshold to $15,000 for preschool subsidies means help reaches more lower- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The upwards review of monthly household income threshold to $15,000 for preschool subsidies means help reaches more lower- and middle-income households.

sections.label: Support for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Prime Minister's announcement that strengthening support for persons with disabilities is a key Government priority and awaits the task force's recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, I welcome Prime Minister Wong's announcement that strengthening support for persons with disabilities is a key priority of the Government and I look forward to the recommendations from the task force that will be reviewing how Singapore can provide more meaningful support at different life stages for persons with disabilities and their families.

sections.label: Support for families and caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker urges the task force to expand support and relief for families and caregivers, including transport, therapy and medical assistive devices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: He is a uniformed officer, protecting our shores.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the task force to expand the support and relief for families and caregivers to alleviate the added pressures across several domains, including transport, therapy and medical assistive devices, among others.

sections.label: ComLink+ social mobility programme
sections.summary: ComLink+, launched in 2023, will see an additional $500 payout for families working towards milestone goals, and the speaker says it is timely for interim findings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: One of Singapore's efforts to tackle social mobility is the ComLink+ programme, which will see an additional $500 payout for families working towards their milestone goals in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the scheme was first launched in 2023 it is timely for the Government to share meaningful interim findings on how ComLink+ is beginning to translate into better educational and social outcomes for the children.

sections.label: AI use in the workforce
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Budget initiatives helping workers use AI to automate routine tasks and asks how the Government will assess AI complementing human intelligence and prevent it widening skill and income gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Budget also highlights initiatives to help workers leverage AI to automate routine tasks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the move and ask how the Government plans to assess how AI complements human intelligence, HI, and not replace critical thought at work and in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: What safeguards are in place to ensure AI does not inadvertently replace individuals or widen skill and income gaps in the workforce?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government could consider collaborating with various key industries to create sector-specific AI toolkits, so talents can effectively conquer AI in their domains.

sections.label: CPF support for seniors
sections.summary: Speaker notes 2027 CPF rate increases for senior workers and more investment options, but asks how Government supports older or medically unfit seniors' CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the young seniors, the planned increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers in 2027 is helpful for retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Providing more investment options for CPF members also offers seniors the opportunity to grow assets, enabling them to age without worry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: But this must come with guardrails and capital preservation at the front and center.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, for older seniors who may face re-employment difficulties or are medically unfit, how will the Government support meaning contributions to their CPF accounts, so that the policy achieves its intended effect?

sections.label: Protections for platform workers
sections.summary: The last term strengthened platform worker protections, advanced progressive wages and made Flexible Work Arrangements a legitimate workplace conversation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In the last term, we strengthened protections for platform workers, advanced progressive wages and made Flexible Work Arrangements a legitimate workplace conversation.

sections.label: Workers never requesting flexibility
sections.summary: NTUC Women and Families surveys found more than half of workers have never made a request.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet in our NTUC Women and Families surveys, more than half of workers have never made a request.

sections.label: Childcare hours for shift workers
sections.summary: Speaker calls for expanded flexible and extended childcare, including weekend and after-hours pilots, so operating hours reflect shift workers' realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Childcare operating hours, especially in estates with shift workers, must better reflect workforce realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore call for support to expand flexible and extended childcare options, including weekend and after-hours pilots in selected communities.

sections.label: NTUC workplace inclusivity calls
sections.summary: NTUC will promote lactational spaces and expand Better Workplaces, and calls for job redesign funding, benchmarks, childcare options and menopause guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The NTUC Women and Family unit will continue to promote lactational spaces in workplaces and we will continue to expand our NTUC Better Workplaces programme this year to support more companies with their lactation room set-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to: scale job redesign funding and build expertise, especially in non-office based, frontline and shift-based sectors; recognise and benchmark progressive workplaces so inclusivity becomes part of Singapore’s competitive edge; publish sectoral benchmarks on FWA utilisation and career progression outcomes; expand flexible and extended childcare options; provide clearer tripartite guidance on supporting women through perimenopause and menopause as legitimate workplace health matters.

sections.label: Inclusive employment for disabled workers
sections.summary: Speaker urges normalising disability-inclusive employment standards, embedding them in hiring and leadership, and building a national database of inclusive employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We must strengthen upstream support in placement and upskilling even in our schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I support initiatives such as the SG Enable Enabling Mark, which recognises disability-inclusive employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It must not remain something that companies aspire to do just once a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It must be normalised as a workplace standard with adequate funding and resourcing, embedded into hiring practices, job design, leadership key performance indicators and organisational culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Employers who invest in inclusive employment should see it reflected in how we assess opportunities and competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: And importantly, we should build a national database of inclusive employers, a live resource base for job seekers with disabilities and their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Apart from FWAs, NTUC has secured stronger protections against workplace discrimination and I am glad that this helps to level the playing field for our working persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We are also working with tripartite partners on a Tripartite Advisory on Reasonable Accommodations to provide guidance on good practices that employers can adopt to make their workplaces more inclusive for persons with disabilities.

sections.label: NTWU electric bus training
sections.summary: The National Transport Workers Union has begun training on electric buses and autonomous driving with public bus operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: To this end, the National Transport Workers Union (NTWU) has already begun training on electric buses and autonomous driving with public bus operators.

sections.label: Analysing job structures for AI
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to invest more resources in analysing job structures and identifying AI-assisted and human functions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If we do not understand the true content of job roles, we may make the wrong judgement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, I call upon the Government to invest more resources in analysing job structures of various industries, clearly identify which functions can be assisted by AI and which must be completed by humans.

sections.label: Family support timing and coverage
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a published review, a ComLink+ coverage target and coach plan, and an explanation why April 2026 is not feasible, citing declining marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Every family the Government has acknowledged as deserving support through fee cap reduction, through expanded subsidy thresholds and through ComLink+ design, should receive that support well with predictability, without arbitrary age cut-offs, without a nine-month gap between announcement and delivery, and not only if they happen to be among the 10,000 families with a coach already assigned to them, The three asks I have made today are specific and proportionate, a published review of whether the structure of support for families with post-primary school age children is well matched to the cost they actually bear; a stated coverage target and coach investment plan for ComLink+; and for the last point, an explanation on why April 2026 is not feasible as a start date, and if the gap cannot be closed, a transitional bridging measure from families who are caught waiting using instruments that the Government has deployed before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just this week, The Straits Times reported that 2025 recorded the lowest number of marriages in Singapore since 2020, a third consecutive year of decline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)

sentences.text: Major high stakes examinations long, a mainstay of gauging student understanding and evaluating student performance, will be less relevant in an AI age.

sentences.text: Agent AI can already accurately execute a wide range of tasks that new graduates used to fill, which means that firms will have a far weaker incentive for hiring them.

sections.label: Autonomous universities and global rankings

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Let us also embrace neurological and intellectual diversity, starting from the ground up with our educational system.

sentences.text: We have a comprehensive China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (CSFTA) which allows the majority of our export to China to enter tariff-free.

sections.label: Johore zone and FTAs
sections.summary: The Government is pushing businesses to consider the Singapore-Johore Special Economic Zone, and Singapore now has 28 implemental FTAs including ASEAN FTA, RCEP and CPTPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government is also pushing for businesses to consider stepping up at the Singapore-Johore Special Economic Zone, which is a natural and logical move, given our proximity, our familiarity, as well as our complementarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Singapore now has 28 implemental FTAs, including multilateral agreements, such as the ASEAN FTA, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.

sections.label: Funds for overseas expansion
sections.summary: Overseas expansions carry risks and need patient capital, so the speaker welcomes the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund and $1.5 billion Financial Sector Development Fund from Budget 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Overseas expansions carry significant risks and often demand patient capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I welcome the $1.5 billion Anchor Fund and $1.5 billion Financial Sector Development Fund announced in Budget 2026.

sections.label: Budget surpluses and rising expenditure
sections.summary: The passage asks how Singapore recorded a $15.1 billion surplus in FY2025 and a projected $8.5 billion surplus in FY2026 despite rising expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As the Budget debate is about financial policy of the Government, the elephant in the room question is of course how is it that despite rising expenditures over the years, Singapore recorded significant surplus of $15.1 billion in FY2025, with a projected $8.5 billion surplus in FY2026?

sections.label: Corporate income tax revenue rise
sections.summary: Corporate income tax rose from $30.1 billion in FY2024 to $35.2 billion in FY2025 and is projected at $37.8 billion in FY2026, driven by growth and BEPS Pillar 2 taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Corporate income tax rose from $30.1 billion from FY2024 to $35.2 billion in FY2025 – the revised figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And it is projected to rise to $37.8 billion in FY2026, an increase of roughly one-third over three years, driven by stronger-than-expected growth and the implementation of the BEPS Pillar 2 top-up taxes.

sections.label: Clarification on continued high surpluses
sections.summary: The passage seeks clarification from the Prime Minister and Minister of Finance on whether high surpluses will continue or greater volatility is expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Given that corporate income tax revenue is expected to remain elevated, I would like to seek clarification from the Prime Minister and the Minister of Finance whether we are likely to see continued high surpluses for the remainder of this five-year term or should we expect greater volatility going forward?

sections.label: Taxing rich and fiscal strength
sections.summary: The passage states lower- and middle-income families pay a GST rate of 7% or below and asks why not tax the rich or foreigners more to redistribute to those households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Taken together, the lower- and the middle-income families effectively pays a GST rate that is 7% or below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I ask myself why would we not want to tax more from the rich or the foreigners who are here to spend more, and then use the financial resources to distribute it to the lower- and the middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is precisely because we remained in the position of physical strength that we are able to allocate meaningful resources across these three pillars: social development, economic growth and security in support of our long-term nation building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Prudent stewardship over the years has provided the Government with the capacity not only to respond to immediate challenges but also to invest strategically in our collective future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our strong fiscal position put us in good stead to confront emerging risks, seize new opportunities, safeguard Singapore's continued progress for generations to come.

sections.label: Exclusions for children of unmarried parents
sections.summary: The passage lists that children of unmarried parents miss the $11,000 Baby Bonus Cash Gift, family nucleus recognition, Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One, their unmarried parent does not receive the Baby Bonus Cash Gift of $11,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Two, they are not recognised as part of a "family nucleus" for HDB schemes, they receive lower subsidies than the family grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Three, their unmarried parent is excluded from the most substantive tax benefits we provide for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They cannot claim the Parenthood Tax Rebate of up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They are not eligible for Working Mother’s Child Relief, even if the unmarried mother has to work doubly hard to bring up her child.

sections.label: Subsidies without working mother criteria
sections.summary: The passage proposes granting childcare and afterschool care subsidies to all students and dropping the working mother criteria, including early intervention and assistive technology subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us grant the additional subsidies for childcare and afterschool care to all students and drop the working mother criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Again, I do not believe that this will overnight make all of our working mothers wake up and decide to stop work, or this encourage those who are looking for work to not continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And this will include additional subsidy for the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children, subsidies for Special Student Care Centres, subsidies for children who need assistive technology and devices, like hearing aids.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the point where theycame to me, they had spent more than one and a half years since they started the ASA process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Why the need to wait another nine more months to start the process, and why then the need to reassess them for adoption suitability, when things are going well with the first child?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And to compound the situation, compared to maternity leave of 16 weeks, adoption leave for parents is only 12 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, I urge all the relevant Government agencies and there are many involved in the process as I have described, to come together, work towards streamlining the process for parents significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And may I suggest that during the period where the child is in Singapore on a Dependent's Pass, let us extend the Singapore Citizenship subsidies for infant care, for childcare, for medicals to the child, because it is a matter of time that they will become a citizen, and these are critical developmental years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Let us not lose time and also let us align the adoption leave with maternity leave at 16 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MOE replied that for PSLE, at least nine in 10 students achieved AL6 or better in English, Mother Tongue, Math and Science; and for the "O" levels, about nine in 10 obtain a C6 or better in English, Mother Tongue and Math.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the latest PISA 2022 assessment of 15-year-olds, 41% of our students were classified as top performers for Math, 24% for Science, and 23% for reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In comparison, for the OECD, it was 9% classified top performers for Math, 7% each for Science and reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If 40% of our cohort are considered top performers in Math globally, then the performance on the national exams should reflect as such – 40% of the cohort should get the top or top two grades in Math.

sections.label: National exams and AI
sections.summary: The speaker says national exams should assess competency, and warns AI may impact foundational knowledge and cognitive skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The role of national exams should be to assess for competency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Foo, I am enjoying your speech, but you have a minute left.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: I believe this will be especially critical for generations to come with the advent of AI, because my concern is that the acquisition of foundational knowledge and fundamental cognitive skills will be impacted by growing up with AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Already, there have been studies that suggest that Gen Z may be the first generation that shows lower average intelligence quotient (IQ) and cognitive scores than previous generations for attention, memory and literacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: This is linked to screen time, digital devices and social media – and I have no doubt that AI will compound these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: In this context, it becomes even more critical that our students achieve fundamental competencies, and the most important factor for this is motivation.

sections.label: AI and cognitive development
sections.summary: Without a foundation, AI may only serve to retard cognitive development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Without this foundation, AI may only serve to retard the cognitive development instead.

sections.label: Singapore exports and exemptions
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gan said that without exemptions, Singapore's exports could face higher duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Gan noted earlier this week, if exemptions are not secured, Singapore's exports, such as pharmaceuticals to semiconductors to advanced manufacturing, could face higher duties.

sections.label: India AI investment ambitions
sections.summary: India has announced ambitions to attract up to US$200 billion in AI and data centre investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: India has announced ambitions to attract up to US$200 billion in AI and data centre investments.

sections.label: Anchoring AI in strong sectors
sections.summary: Anchoring AI in strong sectors and scaling with measurable outcomes creates higher value roles, resilient careers and wage growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we anchor AI in sectors where we are strong, such as mentioned, as advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics, financial services and healthcare, and scale to more sectors with measurable outcomes, we create higher value roles, more resilient careers and stronger wage growth.

sections.label: Pooled AI engineers and modules
sections.summary: The passage proposes evolving CTO-as-a-service to AI-Capability-as-a-Service and pooling resources to co-develop plug-and-play AI modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: First, evolve CTO-as-a-service towards AI-Capability-as-a-Service with pooled AI engineers deployed across SME clusters for hands-on implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Second, organise pooled resources by industry to co-develop plug-and-play AI modules with industry leaders for generic processes, such as quality control, logistics optimisation and predictive maintenance.

sections.label: Gini, wages, senior re-employment
sections.summary: Post-tax-and-transfer Gini fell from about 0.47 in the mid-2000s to around 0.37 today, with re-employment age rising to 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Our post-tax-and-transfer Gini coefficient has fallen from about 0.47 in the mid-2000s to around 0.37 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Real incomes at the 20th percentile have grown faster than the median, supported by Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model and OECD studies indicate relatively strong intergenerational mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: For senior workers, the re-employment age will rise to 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Senior Employment Credit and CPF Transition Offset support retention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Job Redesign Grant helps firms redesign roles.

sections.label: Wayfinding trial, scaling, cybersecurity
sections.summary: A wayfinding trial for visually impaired residents used indoor positioning and AI image recognition, raising questions on scaling and cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Recently, I trialed a project with visually impaired residents to test a wayfinding solution using indoor positioning and AI image recognition to navigate complex indoor spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But how do we connect such projects to agencies, funding and testbeds and scale them with less friction?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We may need a clearer pathway linking community innovators, GovTech, IMDA, healthcare institutions and social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As digital adoption deepens, cybersecurity and scam prevention must keep pace.

sections.label: AI strategy for better lives
sections.summary: AI must strengthen industries, uplift SMEs, empower seniors, open doors for graduates and protect the vulnerable, translating into better lives and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: AI must strengthen industries, uplift SMEs, empower seniors, open doors for graduates and protect the vulnerable, among many others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Above all, our strategy must translate into better lives and good jobs that are higher value, skills-based, fairly paid and future resilient.

sections.label: Support for ComLink+ enhancement
sections.summary: The speaker supports enhancing ComLink+, a scheme helping families progress from public rental towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, I support the enhancement of ComLink+, which is a scheme that helps families progress from public rental towards home ownership.

sections.label: Tapering support after ComLink+
sections.summary: The speaker asks MSF how support is tapered when families transition out of ComLink+ and whether family coaches can help with transition plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: If we want families genuinely to take the difficult step from rental to ownership, or from assistance to self-reliance, we should make the transition predictable and safe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) can share how support is tapered when these families transition out of ComLink+ and whether their family coaches can help with a transition plan, so they do not fall into gaps between schemes at their most vulnerable and most fragile moments of the transition.

sections.label: Micro-SME feedback and PARF rebate
sections.summary: The speaker urges feedback channels for micro-SMEs, and notes the PARF rebate will be reduced by 45% and its cap lowered to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This means a substantial segment of the micro-SMEs may not be in the room when these policy feedback are being gathered, even though they are the ones who are most sensitive to cost and compliance changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I therefore urge the Government to consider opening feedback channels you hear from these small and micro-SMEs, via channels, such as the SME Centres, so that in all fairness, the policy does not get shaped mainly by the larger companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: As announced, the PARF rebate will be reduced by 45% and the cap lowered from $60,000 to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This change applies to Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) obtained from the second COE bidding exercise in February 2026 onwards.

sections.label: New car dealers and COE concerns
sections.summary: An MP asks whether the Government considered impacts on new-car dealers' stock, COE renewals, EV charging readiness and trust when taking away value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fourth, did the Government consider the impact on new-car sellers who typically commit to inventory and order pipelines six to 12 months in advance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For these new car dealers, they are now at risk of holding stock that is much harder to sell and may have a knock-out effect on their business viability and also employees' jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fifth, did the Government expect this change to increase COE renewals because retaining older cars becomes relatively more attractive and if so, what is the expected impact on the number of COEs available for the new cars and the resulting trajectory of the COE premiums?

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For example, is the national power grid ready to support a mass adoption of EVs, and will EV charging, especially in older estates, keep in pace, so Singaporeans will not feel that policy is moving faster than practical realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But when the Government takes away value, it can be immediate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I worry this perception would erode trust, especially if ordinary families are hurt because they are not sophisticated buyers and reasonably expect the rules to remain stable when making big purchases.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extended
sections.summary: The Government provides employers a Senior Employment Credit for seniors who wish to keep working, extended another year in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If seniors wish to continue working, the Government provides employers with a Senior Employment Credit, which has been extended for another year under this year's Budget.

sections.label: Seniors living alone by 2030
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee on Ageing estimates 83,000 seniors above 65 will live alone by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Ministerial Committee on Ageing, an estimated 83,000 seniors above 65 years will live alone by the year 2030.

sections.label: Older residents' education levels
sections.summary: Department of Statistics Population Trends 2025 shows nearly 40% of those over 55 had below secondary education as at 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics Population trends 2025, as at 2024, nearly 40% of those over 55 years old, have education at below secondary level – a very significant segment.

sections.label: Hougang HDB branch closure
sections.summary: Hougang HDB Branch closed 1 September for an integrated development, with counter services replaced by electronic and self-service machines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): The HDB Branch Office at Hougang Central closed on 1 September, affecting areas, including Hougang Single Member Constituency and parts of Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In response to the related issue raised in Parliament by Hougang Member of Parliament (MP) Dennis Tan, the Ministry of National Development responded that the Hougang Branch closed on 1 September to make way for the development of an integrated commercial and residential project in the vicinity of Hougang Avenue 10 and Hougang Central.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, HDB has not established a new physical branch nearby, but has replaced counter services with electronic service and self-service machines.

sections.label: Means testing affects seniors' support
sections.summary: Means testing for Silver Support and CHAS subsidies can reduce or remove seniors' support if a wage-earning child lives with them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Take, for instance, the means testing criteria for Government subsidies and schemes, the Silver Support Scheme and healthcare subsidies for long-term care and outpatient treatment under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) are prime examples of policies affecting seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should a wage-earning adult child decide to live with his or her parents for mutual support, the seniors may become ineligible for support or have support reduced compared to if they lived on their own.

sections.label: Per capita income criterion
sections.summary: It asks whether the per capita household income criterion for schemes like Silver Support could be replaced by looking at seniors' own income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it be possible for instance, to do away with the per capita household income criterion for schemes, such as Silver Support, and simply look at the seniors' own income?

sections.label: Harmonised medical examination report scheme
sections.summary: Under the harmonised medical examination report scheme implemented on 2 February, drivers need only one medical examination usable by both agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some have also had difficulties uploading the medical reports onto the portals of the two agencies, as they were not comfortable handling attachments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Now, under the new harmonised medical examination report scheme implemented on 2 February, drivers need only attend one medical examination that can be used by both agencies.

sections.label: AI education and ITE in North
sections.summary: It states that infrastructure must support keen learners and that the speaker previously suggested establishing another ITE in the North.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As our nation ramps up efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) education and encourages lifelong learning, we must ensure that the right infrastructure is in place to support every keen learner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I have previously suggested in this House that we consider establishing another Institute of Technical Education (ITE) in the North.

sections.label: Infertility in Singapore
sections.summary: It states that SingHealth statistics indicate roughly one in six couples, about 17%, experience infertility in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The struggles they face are deeply personal, often invisible and sometimes painful." SingHealth statistics indicate that roughly one in six couples, about 17%, experience infertility in Singapore.

sections.label: Fertility and ART recommendations
sections.summary: It lists PAP Women's Wing MPs' recommendations on fertility screenings, ART subsidies, MediSave limits, private clinic co-funding and workplace support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My fellow PAP Women's Wing MPs and I stand aligned with FSS' recommendations to propose several feasible solutions to create those "right conditions": one, promote early health screenings for fertility, potentially collaborating with the Registry of Marriages and as part of the Healthy SG movement; two, increased subsidies for assisted reproductive treatments (ART); three, raising the MediSave utilisation limit for ART and allowing treatments in private clinics to alleviate long waiting times in public hospitals where time is of the essence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Additionally, we recommend Government to co-fund for ART at private clinics, expanding MediSave withdrawals from three to six cycles, MediSave coverage for elective egg freezing, subsidised fertility screenings for couples and enhanced workplace support for fertility and family-building.

sections.label: Housing, childcare and working mothers
sections.summary: It describes residents' housing obstacles and urges priority for larger flats, flexible CDA use and reinstated working mother tax incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Obstacles that my residents face include successfully balloting for a HDB flat, upgrading to a larger flat to accommodate their growing family, which for buyers of resale flats means needing to fork out at times significant cash to meet the cash-over-valuation component.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As such, I hope that HDB can provide access to bigger HDB flats by granting priority as second timers to the Sale of Balance Flats for families with two or more children who wish to upgrade and live closer to or with their parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For children’s education, we must keep expenses affordable by offering better flexibility in tapping on the Child Development Account (CDA) funds for preschool-recommended enrichment lessons and field trips, for example.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We should also support continuous career progression for working parents, especially mothers, ensuring stable incomes to cover growing expenses for ageing parents and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I urge reinstating the working mother tax incentives to allow mothers who earned more income each year to claim a larger amount of tax relief for each child, so as to motivate mothers to remain and/or return to the workforce when they feel ready to pursue leadership positions.

sections.label: Frailty programme and LPA fees
sections.summary: A frailty programme in Woodgrove and Marsiling is cited, with calls to waive LPA fees and revamp the Wills Registry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A recent example is the Frailty Management Programme that was launched in Care Corner Active Ageing Centres in Woodgrove and Marsiling, with a comprehensive and tailored care plan and close monitoring to address our seniors’ physical, nutritional and social needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But I believe more can be done to increase the take-up rates, especially among our seniors, such as: one, continuing to waive the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) registration fees for Singaporeans; and two, considering a revamp of the Wills Registry, while ensuring users are properly advised by legal professionals and better protected.

sections.label: AI strategy adoption focus
sections.summary: The speaker says AI fiscal levers focus on adoption, which risks transferring value to foreign technology companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Right now, the heavy ﬁscal levers in our AI strategy are largely focused towards adoption – identifying where AI can improve our existing industries and subsidising our businesses to deploy it faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If our industrial strategy remains focused on fast adoption, we are agreeing to a permanent, compounding transfer of value to foreign technology companies.

sections.label: Edge AI global export niche
sections.summary: The speaker argues for Edge AI and its efficiency research as a niche with global export potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We must now look further aﬁeld with global ambitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I want to make the case for another niche, one with global export potential – Edge AI and the efﬁciency research that underpins it.

sections.label: Edge AI as RIE2030 priority
sections.summary: The speaker asks that Edge AI efficiency research be an explicit RIE2030 priority, measured by commercial export potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has already committed $37 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 (RIE2030) plan, with AI explicitly within the scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask that within that envelope, Edge AI efﬁciency research – model distillation, quantisation and on-device deployment – be named as an explicit priority, with success measured by commercial export potential and not just domestic adoption.

sections.label: Stanford ADP entry-level hiring study
sections.summary: A Stanford and ADP study found US entry-level hiring in AI-exposed sectors fell 16% since late 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Research published in October last year by Stanford University and ADP found that since late 2022, which was when ChatGPT broke cover, entry-level hiring in AI-exposed sectors in the US has fallen by 16%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For software developers aged 22 to 25 speciﬁcally, the headcount has fallen by a greater 20%.

sections.label: Publishing graduate employment data
sections.summary: The speaker calls on MOM to publish granular employment data for new graduates by sector, role and AI exposure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We cannot manage what we do not measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I call on MOM to publish granular employment data for new graduates, broken down by sector, role type and AI exposure levels.

sections.label: EIS deduction graduate roles
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to require firms claiming the EIS deduction above a threshold to show a credible plan for maintaining graduate and entry level roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While the details are being firmed up, I ask that the Government require that firms claiming the EIS deduction above a meaningful threshold demonstrate a credible plan for maintaining graduate and entry level roles, not by preserving roles that AI has genuinely made redundant, but by investing and reimagining what junior work looks like in an AI-augmented firm.

sections.label: Lowering qualifying age to 35
sections.summary: The speaker says lowering the qualifying age to 35 is a simple, concrete and targeted step addressing where the disruption is occurring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lowering the qualifying age to 35 is a simple, concrete and targeted step that addresses where the disruption is actually occurring.

sections.label: Targeted retraining tax credit
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a targeted retraining tax credit available only to firms that reskilled a specific worker into an AI-augmented role rather than retrenching them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: AI makes substitution easier than it has ever been.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I propose a targeted retraining tax credit, available only to firms that can demonstrate that they have reskilled a specific worker into an AI-augmented role rather than retrenching them.

sections.label: Annual AI gains audit
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an annual AI gains audit scoped to the four sectors receiving public support in the national AI Missions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government is investing taxpayer resources and regulatory sandboxes in four national AI Missions: advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These are the right priorities, but they come with a public obligation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I propose that an annual AI gains audit, scoped specifically to these four sectors, be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Not red tape for every business, but a targeted accountability mechanism for sectors receiving extraordinary levels of public support to answer one straightforward question: are the productivity gains from state-backed AI Missions flowing into the wages of our workers or are they flowing into shareholder returns?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The strategic advantage of AI must be felt in the wages of our workers, not just in the earnings reports of the companies deploying the technology.

sections.label: MOH operating expenditure
sections.summary: In this Budget, MOH's operating expenditure is about $20 billion, and healthcare spending has more than doubled over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) operating expenditure is about $20 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, healthcare spending has more than doubled.

sections.label: Budget 2026 balance
sections.summary: Budget 2026 reflects a balance of investing where necessary, strengthening fiscal structures and financing mechanisms, and keeping the system strong for this and the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 reflects that balance investing where necessary, strengthening fiscal structures and our financing mechanisms, and ensuring that our system remains strong not only for this generation, but for the next.

sections.label: Budget 2026 healthcare direction
sections.summary: Budget 2026 strengthens healthcare through Healthier SG enrolment, primary care reinforcement, and expanded community and long-term care capacity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 strengthens this direction through Healthier SG enrolment, primary care reinforcement, and expanded community and long-term care capacity.

sections.label: Community rehabilitation and home recovery
sections.summary: Strengthening community rehabilitation and home-based recovery improves patient outcomes and system efficiency, and can be refined by shortening time-to-rehabilitation, boosting community therapy capacity and tracking functional outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Strengthening community rehabilitation and home-based recovery therefore improves both patient outcomes and system efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It ensures that our investment in acute medicine delivers full value.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can continue refining this by shortening time-to-rehabilitation after discharge, strengthening community therapy capacity and tracking functional outcomes to ensure quality and accountability.

sections.label: Capacity and coherence in healthcare
sections.summary: Better access and shorter waits require strengthening capacity and coherence, with responsibilities organised around training and competency to reduce duplication and ease bottlenecks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
