sentences.text: If we want better access and shorter waits, we must strengthen not only capacity, but coherence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: When responsibilities are organised clearly around training and competency, duplication reduces, bottlenecks ease and patients move more smoothly through the system.

sections.label: Elderly fear becoming a burden
sections.summary: Tengah residents said many elderly fear becoming a burden to families, and the speaker supports Government efforts in MediSave, subsidies and long-term care support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In conversations with residents in Tengah, I found that what many elderly people fear most is not their own suffering, but becoming a burden to their families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support the Government's continued efforts in MediSave, subsidies and long-term care support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The best healthcare is not only about treating illness after it occurs, but about preventing disease, promoting early recovery and reducing avoidable hospital stays.

sections.label: Kampong Glam rent increases
sections.summary: A CNA report showed median yearly rent in Kampong Glam rose 25% from 2023 to 2025, and high rents in Haji and Bali Lanes may spill over to Arab Street, thinning heritage businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 12 January, a report by CNA revealed that between 2023 and 2025, the yearly median rent in Kampong Glam rose from $6.02 to $7.54 per square foot, translating to a 25% increase over two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During our Sitting earlier this month, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for National Development confirmed that a small proportion of tenants did face rental hikes of 25% or more in these two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He, however, said that this involved leases for shops in high footfall streets, such as Haji and Bali Lanes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: High rents in Haji and Bali Lanes can easily have a spillover effect on other adjacent streets, such as Arab Street, which houses some traditional textile retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The disappearance of heritage businesses in Kampong Glam will be an irreversible thinning of the precinct's place meaning.

sections.label: Heritage business licences proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether parameters could be amended, such as introducing heritage business licences for historic districts, to keep heritage businesses viable and prevent over-commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it not be possible to amend these parameters to ensure that heritage businesses can remain viable in the areas, such as introducing heritage business licences, specifically for historic districts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would offer businesses some measure of protection from open market competition, as well as prevent the over-commercialisation of a historic district.

sections.label: National Archives declassification access
sections.summary: In 2023, metadata of around 780,000 records was made public and 68,000 filed records were declassified, with automatic declassification planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2023, the then Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information mentioned that the NAS has made the metadata of around 780,000 records available to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Senior Minister of State's statement, it was also revealed that 68,000 filed records have been declassified and made accessible to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An automatic declassification process will make records generally available to the public by default instead of requiring interested Singaporeans and researchers to undertake an opaque approval process to gain access.

sections.label: AI development and use rules
sections.summary: The Prime Minister reassured that the Government will define how AI is developed and used in Singapore, including clear rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is how we develop our sense of judgement and our capacity for creativity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I appreciate the Prime Minister's reassurance that the Government will define how AI is developed and used in Singapore, including setting out clear rules for its responsible and safe implementation.

sections.label: Data centre energy and sustainability
sections.summary: Data centres used 7% of Singapore's energy in 2020, a moratorium was issued in 2019 and lifted from 2022, and IMDA released a Green Data Centre Roadmap in May 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Locally, data centres accounted for 7% of Singapore's total energy usage in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, data centres also contribute to the urban heating of our island, because for every one megawatt of heat removed from data centres by the cooling systems, 1.2 megawatt of heat is ejected into the environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, resource and sustainability concerns prompted the Government to issue a moratorium on data centre construction in 2019, which has been lifted in phases since 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In May 2024, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) released the Green Data Centre Roadmap, which established energy and water efficiency targets for data centres for the next 10 years.

sections.label: Changed world and growth forecast
sections.summary: It is presented when the Prime Minister described a profoundly changed world, with growth expected to moderate to between 2% and 4% this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is presented at a moment when the Prime Minister has described a profoundly changed world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, growth is expected to moderate to between 2% and 4%.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary and PWCS
sections.summary: The Local Qualifying Salary will rise to $1,800, and the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme will be enhanced and extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Local Qualifying Salary will rise to $1,800.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Credit Scheme will be enhanced and extended.

sections.label: Preschool and ComLink+ subsidies
sections.summary: Preschool subsidies will extend to families earning up to $15,000, and ComLink+ enhancements can provide around $10,000 annually for families with young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Preschool subsidies will extend to families earning up to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: ComLink+ enhancements can provide around $10,000 annually for families with young children.

sections.label: Corporate volunteering and ESG reporting
sections.summary: Corporate volunteering and social contribution metrics can be integrated into ESG reporting frameworks, encouraging private-sector ownership of nation-building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Corporate volunteering and social contribution metrics can be integrated into environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting frameworks, encouraging deeper private-sector ownership of nation-building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A "we first" society must be cultivated intentionally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Unity must be measurable, participation must be meaningful and contribution must be normalised.

sections.label: Mirxes Hong Kong IPO
sections.summary: Mirxes IPO-ed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, raising HK$1.09 billion, because SGX has no equivalent pathway for pre-revenue biotech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On that day, Mirxes, a microRNA cancer diagnostics biotech company incubated over many years of Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) research at Biopolis IPO-ed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEX), raising HK$1.09 billion with China-linked cornerstone investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mirxes listed in Hong Kong, not Singapore, because the Singapore Exchange (SGX) has no equivalent to the HKEX pathway for pre-revenue biotech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Its cornerstone investors were Chinese entities holding over 40% of the IPO.

sections.label: Agencies structured as grant givers
sections.summary: The structural flaw is that agencies like EDB and the Statutory Boards are structured as grant givers, not investors or ecosystem builders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The structural flaw is that agencies like the Economic Development Board (EDB) and the Statutory Boards are structured as grant givers, not as investors or ecosystem builders.

sections.label: Fragmented landscape and SG Growth Capital
sections.summary: The fragmented landscape leaves no entity with mandate, capital or authority for large bets, though the SG Growth Capital merger is a step forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Each has a logic, but the aggregate effect is a landscape so fragmented that no single entity has the mandate, the capital concentration or the institutional authority to make the kind of large, decisive fast bets that define successful deep tech commercialisation elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The SG Growth Capital merger of SEEDS and EDBI is a step in the right direction, but the deeper question is whether we have the institutional courage to truly consolidate to give one to two entities the capital, the mandate and critically, the permission to fail, at scale, rather than spreading accountability so thin that no one is responsible for ecosystem outcomes.

sections.label: France merges bodies into Bpifrance
sections.summary: Under Hollande and Macron in 2012, France merged four fragmented investment bodies into a single entity, Bpifrance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under Francois Hollande and economic advisor Emmanuel Macron, in 2012, France merged four fragmented investment bodies – one for SME loans, guarantees innovation, one for venture capital, one for strategic equity and one for regional equity – into a single entity, Bpifrance.

sections.label: Bpifrance 10-year assessment
sections.summary: Bpifrance's 10-year assessment found 80% of funded French startups got its support, and it accepts below-market returns to build the ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Its 10-year assessment found that 80% of French startups that raised funds between 2013 and 2021 received Bpifrance support, and two thirds of French venture capital funds have Bpifrance as a limited partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Bpifrance deliberately accepts below market returns, targeting 7% annually rather than 10% plus to take risk that private investors will not, training a generation of entrepreneurs and building an ecosystem from scratch.

sections.label: Deep tech visa proposal
sections.summary: Proposes an 18-month engagement with a materials engineer or combustion engine specialist and a company-driven deep tech visa tied to company credentials, not income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An 18-month engagement with a materials engineer or a combustion engine specialist can redefine a company's trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose a segmented approach: a company-driven deep tech visa, tied not to income, but the company's credentials.

sections.label: Israel Taiwan Korea IP rules
sections.summary: Describes Israel's binding conditions on public R&D funding, ITRI's 1987 TSMC spin-off, and South Korea's National Core Technologies export approval rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Law for the Encouragement of Industrial Research and Development, the Israel Innovation Authority attaches binding conditions to all public R&D funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: IP developed with public grants cannot be transferred outside Israel without explicit prior approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Industrial Technology Research Institute spun off Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company in 1987, by transferring fabs, equipment, technologies and 98 professionals to a new Taiwanese entity – with significant government ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Industrial Technology Protection Act, South Korea designates more than 70 technologies across 13 fields as National Core Technologies – semiconductors, displays, batteries – and requires prior approval for any export or merger and acquisitions involving these technologies.

sections.label: Offshore IP transfer approval law
sections.summary: Proposes legislating that IP developed with public R&D funding cannot be permanently transferred offshore without prior approval, enforceable against Singapore entities and individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Legislate that IP developed with public R&D funding cannot be permanently transferred offshore without prior approval from a designated authority – enforceable domestically against Singapore-domiciled entities and individuals.

sections.label: Lack of coordination and integration
sections.summary: States that what she lacked was better coordination and integration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: What she lacked was just better coordination and integration.

sections.label: AIC and care integration efforts
sections.summary: Cites AIC, regional health systems, community care and Age Well SG as showing foresight, and notes integration underway through care coordinators and transitional care programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The formation of the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), the development of regional health systems, expansion of community care and ageing in place initiatives, like the Age Well SG, demonstrate our strong foresight and the sustained effort by the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the whole of Government.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Integration is already underway through care coordinators, transitional care programmes and stronger partnerships across primary, acute and community care sectors.

sections.label: Case worker for complex patients
sections.summary: States that patients with complex needs were assigned a single case worker supported by a multidisciplinary team of doctors, nurses, social workers and allied health professionals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Patients with complex needs were assigned a single case worker, supported by a multidisciplinary team, which included doctors, nurses, social workers and other allied health professionals.

sections.label: Piloting integrated help in regional health systems
sections.summary: Proposes piloting help from when need is recognised, using Healthier SG networks, care coordinators, digital records and community partners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: True integration begins when help starts the moment the need for that help is recognised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This can be piloted progressively within our regional health systems, leveraging our Healthier SG networks, existing care coordinators, shared digital records, community partners, including our community health posts.

sections.label: Training mosque officers and senior programmes
sections.summary: Sets out three steps: training mosque officers and volunteers, placing social health coordination officers at mosques, and expanding senior citizen programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, enhancing training and resources for mosque officers and volunteers so that they can work more closely with the health and social services sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, placing social health coordination officers at mosques that are more frequently attended by senior citizens so that assistance can be better accessed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Third, expanding senior citizen programmes at mosques to include health talks, health screenings and counselling support.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and senior employment
sections.summary: States two needs: creating more lifelong learning opportunities and expanding meaningful employment opportunities for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, we must create more opportunities that encourages lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, we must expand on meaningful employment opportunities for seniors.

sections.label: Life expectancy, inflation and senior support
sections.summary: Notes life expectancy of about 83.5 years, food, healthcare and transport inflation of about 60% to 80%, and government cash and voucher support for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Our life expectancy in Singapore has risen over the years to about 83.5 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: During this 20-year period, if we use the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS’) goods and services inflation calculator, a basket of goods and services under the food, healthcare and transport categories which, in my view, are three categories that affect seniors significantly, increased approximately between 60% to 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Accordingly, the Government has over the years supplemented our seniors in retirement with cash and voucher support in various forms: CPF and MediSave top-ups, Silver Support and the Pioneer, Merdeka and Majulah Packages.

sections.label: Rising one-person senior households
sections.summary: States one-person households aged 65 and above more than doubled from 42,100 in 2014 to 87,200 in 2024 and expects the trend to grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics, the number of one-person households for those aged 65 years and above has more than doubled from 2014 to 2024, rising from 42,100 to 87,200 households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Based on the overall expectation that one in four Singaporeans will be over the age of 65 by 2030, we can certainly expect this trend to continue to grow.

sections.label: Public Guardian and Mental Capacity Act review
sections.summary: Explains the Public Guardian cannot intervene directly when a senior without a viable deputy loses mental capacity, and asks if the Act will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Currently, the Public Guardian can only supervise or investigate matters involving LPAs and or deputyships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Under certain circumstances, the Public Guardian may appoint suitable third parties, like social workers or medical care providers as professional deputies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Mental Capacity Act, however, does not empower the Public Guardian to intervene directly if a senior loses his or her mental capacity and has no viable person who can be appointed as a deputy to make decisions and manage matters on his or her behalf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This could result in vulnerable seniors failing to get the support or timely intervention they need, even with many willing helping hands in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I ask if the Government will consider reviewing the Mental Capacity Act and empowering the Public Guardian to intervene directly in such cases?

sections.label: Australia Aged Care Act 2024
sections.summary: Australia's rights-based Aged Care Act 2024 came into force on 1 November 2025, focusing on seniors' rights, needs and choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Interestingly, Australia also recently enacted the rights-based Aged Care Act 2024 which came into force on 1 November 2025 with a focus on empowering seniors to uphold their rights, needs and personal choices in their aged care.

sections.label: Value of unpaid caregiving
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates global unpaid care compensation at roughly $11 trillion, and a 2024 Duke-NUS study values informal caregiving for seniors 75 and above at $1.28 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum estimates compensation of unpaid care labour globally to be in the tune of roughly $11 trillion – 9% of global GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Closer to home, a 2024 Duke-National University of Singapore (NUS) study revealed that informal caregiving for our seniors aged 75 and above is worth $1.28 billion annually, an equivalent to 11% of our total Government expenditure on healthcare, which is today's second after defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Behind every fiscal surplus is an "invisible surplus" provided by our caregivers.

sections.label: Toa Payoh rental flat occupancy
sections.summary: Toa Payoh Central has 17 rental blocks, and the median number of occupants in a two-room rental flat is four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Toa Payoh, we have 17 rental blocks in Toa Payoh Central.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I noted in a Parliamentary Question reply this week that the median number of occupants in a two-room rental flat is four.

sections.label: Income and wealth inequality
sections.summary: Income inequality is at its lowest on record, but wealth inequality has widened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our income inequality is at its lowest on record, but the more insidious wealth inequality has widened.

sections.label: Funding paid caregiving leave
sections.summary: With a $15.1 billion surplus, the fiscal capacity exists to fund paid parent or elder caregiving leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With a $15.1 billion surplus, we have the fiscal capacity to do exactly that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Caregivers often torn between being at work and the bedside, just as childcare leave supports the role of a parent, we must fund paid parent or elder caregiving leave.

sections.label: Upskilling foreign domestic workers
sections.summary: Foreign domestic workers are not required to have the specialised care qualifications that senior care centre staff hold, so geriatric and palliative care upskilling should be subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While staff in senior care centres uphold basic care and nursing competencies, yet when those same seniors requiring specialised care return home at night and on weekends, we do not require our foreign domestic workers to have these similar qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We should subsidise upskilling specialised in geriatric and palliative care.

sections.label: Support for larger families
sections.summary: It calls for increased direct tiered support for families with three or more children to keep large families a strength rather than a driver of household debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If demography is destiny, and families are bucking the trend to hold up our TFR, we must increase direct tiered support for families with three or more children to ensure that the invisible infrastructure of a large family remains a source of strength rather than a driver of household debt.

sections.label: AI and human care
sections.summary: It states AI helps identify vulnerable groups, but every node in the care network must be filled by humans, not cold machine interaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What they "Mai lai" or do not want to come, is that kind of cold interaction that has only graphics on a machine, without human dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We must be clear: AI is the "ladder" that helps us identify vulnerable groups, but every node in the care network must be filled by humans.

sections.label: Three questions on Singapore's future
sections.summary: It asks how economic success and jobs will be secured, whether cost pressures are eased, and whether the fiscal strategy is fit for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, how will we secure continued economic success and good jobs for Singaporeans in a changed world?

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, are we doing enough to ease cost pressures and ensure every Singaporean can progress?

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And third, is our fiscal strategy fit for the future, the challenges we face both now and in the future?

sections.label: US tariffs and small countries
sections.summary: It says US tariff changes show uncertainty is becoming the norm, and smaller countries like Singapore risk being bypassed or marginalised.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We felt these pressures acutely last year, especially after the US' Liberation Day tariffs.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Now, fresh changes in US tariffs remind us that uncertainty and volatility is becoming the norm and in such a world, smaller countries, like Singapore, risk being bypassed or marginalised.

sections.label: Manufacturing share of GDP
sections.summary: It states manufacturing contributed about 20% of GDP on average over the last decade and declined from 14% in 2015 to about 12% today.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, the manufacturing sector has, on average, contributed about 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And it has declined – from 14% in 2015 to about 12% today.

sections.label: F&B and retail declines
sections.summary: It states that between 2019 and 2024, figures fell from 26% to 17% for the F&B sector and from 30% to 26% for retail.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, they fell from 26% to 17% for the F&B sector; and from 30% to 26% for the retail sector.

sections.label: Wages, foreign worker flexibility
sections.summary: The passage states measures to uplift incomes and narrow wage gaps, enhance the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, and consider calibrated flexibility on Work Permit holder sources without relaxing the Dependency Ratio Ceiling.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is the right thing to do – to uplift incomes, strengthen dignity in work and narrow wage gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And at the same time, to support businesses through the transition, we introduced the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and, in this Budget, we are enhancing the Scheme and extending it for another two years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mr Mark Lee asked for more leeway for SMEs to hire foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We cannot relax the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC).

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Doing so will encourage excessive reliance on foreign manpower and weaken our Singaporean core.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we will consider calibrated ways to provide more flexibility, like expanding the sources from which businesses can hire Work Permit holders, for certain types of occupations where genuine shortages exist.

sections.label: AI tools and ASEAN expansion
sections.summary: With Government support, the company is developing AI tools to analyse customer data and shopping behaviour, employs 150 people, and plans to expand into ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And with Government support, it is developing AI tools to analyse customer data and shopping behaviour, so as to enable more personalised product recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And it now employs 150 people and is making plans to expand into ASEAN.

sections.label: Permanent employees and PMET vacancies
sections.summary: Permanent employees rose to nearly 91%, vacancies outnumber jobseekers, and over 40% of openings are entry-level PMET roles.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The proportion of permanent employees has risen to a record high of nearly 91%, with gains across most sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Vacancies continue to outnumber jobseekers and over 40% of openings are entry-level professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMET) roles, indicating still healthy demand for young graduates.

sections.label: No jobless growth, AI strategy
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore will not have jobless growth, will exploit AI to grow the economy, and ensure growth translates into good jobs and better wages.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is our assurance and that is why our strategy going ahead is clear.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will not have jobless growth in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will exploit AI to grow the economy, and we will ensure that growth translates into good jobs and better wages.

sections.label: Rate rose then fell
sections.summary: In Singapore, the rate rose to more than 6% in 2022 and has since come down to 0.9% last year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, it rose to more than 6% in 2022 and it has since come down to 0.9% last year.

sections.label: Household and retiree amounts
sections.summary: A lower-income household with young children is about $5,000, and a retired elderly couple is about $7,600.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A lower-income household with young children – about $5,000.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And a retired elderly couple – about $7,600.

sections.label: One-off versus structural Budget measures
sections.summary: About 5% of the overall Budget is for one-off measures in FY2025 and FY2026, with 95% for longer-term structural schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because the facts are only about 5% of our overall Budget is for one-off measures – that was so in FY2025 and it is so in FY2026.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The remaining 95%, the overwhelming share, is for longer-term and structural schemes.

sections.label: Retirees, incomes and inflation
sections.summary: Retirees face greater impact as they are not working, so more is provided for them in the Budget; incomes rose faster than inflation over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: He highlighted the concerns among seniors and, indeed, one group that will face greater impact is retirees because they are not working and that is why we provide more for them in the Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But when we look at data at both the household and the individual worker levels – household and workers – in fact, incomes have risen faster than inflation over the past decade, across the entire income distribution.

sections.label: AV and PCHI as indicators
sections.summary: AV and PCHI are practical and effective indicators.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: AV and PCHI are practical and effective indicators.

sections.label: Inclusive growth and wage schemes
sections.summary: Without inclusive growth cost pressures would have been worse; the Budget raises the Local Qualifying Salary and enhances and extends the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Without this inclusive growth, I have no doubt that the cost pressures that we are feeling on the ground would have been far worse.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And in this Budget, we are raising the Local Qualifying Salary as well as enhancing and extending the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sections.label: Net wealth of lowest quintile
sections.summary: Households in the lowest quintile today have average net wealth of nearly $300,000, a meaningful foundation.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, households in the lowest quintile have average net wealth of nearly $300,000 – that is a meaningful foundation.

sections.label: CPF interest rates
sections.summary: The CPF provides risk-free returns of 2.5% on the Ordinary Account and 4% on the Special Account, with extra interest of 1% to 2%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The CPF provides, as Members would know, risk-free returns of 2.5% on the Ordinary Account (OA) and 4% on the Special Account (SA), with extra interest of 1% to 2%.

sections.label: CPFIS-OA investor returns
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2024, most CPFIS-OA investors earned above 2.5% per annum, but only about half achieved returns above 4%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2024, while a majority of CPFIS-OA investors earned above 2.5% per annum, only about half achieved returns of more than 4%; this is for OA.

sections.label: CPF Board scheme rollout
sections.summary: The CPF Board will call for expressions of interest next month and aims to roll out the scheme in the first half of 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The CPF Board will be engaging the industry next month to call for expressions of interest.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The CPF Board is working towards rolling out the scheme in the first half of 2028, but if we can do this earlier, we will.

sections.label: ComLink+ families in rental housing
sections.summary: About 11,000 families are on ComLink+, most of whom are in rental housing.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin asked about this particular issue of ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There are, today, about 11,000 families on ComLink+, most are in rental housing.

sections.label: Large Families Scheme payouts
sections.summary: Parents can receive up to $48,000 for a third or fourth child under the Large Families Scheme, with marriage and parenthood expenditure rising from $4 billion in FY2020 to $7 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, we have taken significant steps on both fronts recently.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And with the Large Families Scheme, parents can now receive up to $48,000 for their third or fourth child, and even more for the fifth or subsequent child.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a result of the recent enhancements, our expenditure on marriage and parenthood initiatives has increased – from $4 billion in FY2020 to $7 billion in this Budget.

sections.label: NIRC proposal rejected
sections.summary: The WP suggested raising the maximum Net Investment Returns Contribution from 50% to 60%, but this was not agreed to because the framework safeguards intergenerational equity.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The WP had suggested raising the maximum Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) we can use in the Annual Budget from 50% to 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We did not agree with that proposal, because the NIRC framework was carefully designed to safeguard intergenerational equity.

sections.label: GST increase and mitigation
sections.summary: GST was the only broad-based and sustainable option to fund rising healthcare needs while preserving the reserves framework, with the effective tax increase delayed for most Singaporean households.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the end, the GST was the only broad-based and sustainable option to fund rising healthcare needs, while preserving our reserves framework.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But even as we raised the GST, we also made sure we mitigated the impact on Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We delayed the effective tax increase for the majority of Singaporean households, by at least five years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: After accounting for these measures, the majority of GST collections are and will continue to be, from higher-income households, tourists and foreigners.

sections.label: Corporate tax and top-up taxes
sections.summary: Initial sense is that the further increase from top-up taxes could be significant, based on strong corporate tax collections so far.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Based on the strong corporate tax collections so far – and that is pre top-up taxes – our initial sense is that the further increase from the top-up taxes could be significant.

sections.label: FY2026 Budget expenditure share
sections.summary: For this FY2026 Budget, expenditure is at 18.4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For this FY2026 Budget, expenditure is at 18.4% of GDP.

sections.label: Spending, fiscal position, GST
sections.summary: Spending is likely to exceed 20% of GDP well before 2030, with the fiscal position expected to remain healthy and no further GST increases until at least 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we expect our needs to rise even more for the coming years, in this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, Government spending is likely to exceed 20% of GDP well before 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At this juncture, if circumstances remain broadly stable and without any further major revenue moves, we expect our fiscal position during this term of Government to remain healthy.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have already said that there will be no further GST increases until at least 2030.

sections.label: Updated medium-term projections to 2035
sections.summary: With updated revenue and expenditure developments, updated medium-term projections extending to 2035 will be published by next year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With updated revenue and expenditure developments, these projections will need to be refreshed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will publish updated medium-term projections extending to 2035 by next year.

sections.label: Resident workers and income tax
sections.summary: About one in three resident workers pay no personal income tax, and about eight in 10 of those who do have an effective tax rate under 6%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: When taken together with our progressive tax rates, tax reliefs and rebates, currently about one in three resident workers pay no personal income tax.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Among those who do, about eight in 10 have an effective tax rate of less than 6%.

sections.label: Revenue, reserves and NIRC
sections.summary: Revenue includes significant investment income from reserves, and excluding Net Investment Returns Contribution, expenditure exceeds revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And in Singapore's case, revenue includes significant investment income from our reserves, not just taxes collected from businesses and households.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, if you exclude Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC), expenditure exceeds revenue.

sections.label: Tax paid versus benefits received
sections.summary: The top quintile receives 20 cents in benefits for every dollar of tax paid.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For every dollar of tax paid by the top quintile, they receive 20 cents in benefits.

sections.label: Benefits per dollar of tax
sections.summary: A dollar of tax can return more than $2 in benefits, and the bottom quintile gets $7.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A dollar of tax, you can get back more, $2 in benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And the bottom quintile gets $7 in benefits.

sections.label: Accountability for RIE 2030 spending
sections.summary: It examines how the $37 billion committed to RIE 2030 will be expended and Singaporean jobs enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It just dives straight into the RIE domains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And this is an example of, I think, the sort of accountability people are actually interested in looking at – how or where the $37 billion, which was committed to RIE 2030, how it will be expended, how Singaporean jobs will be enhanced and what opportunities there would be for Singaporean, to say nothing of the budgetary issues.

sections.label: Pillar Two implementation uncertainty
sections.summary: Revenue upsides were expected, but it was unclear then whether Pillar Two would be implemented, lowering downside risk for now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that would give upsides to revenue, but we were not sure at that time whether Pillar Two would be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the downside risk has come down, at least for now.

sections.label: Pillar Two and MNE negotiating power
sections.summary: Jurisdictions including Singapore implement domestic top-up taxes, but MNEs still have considerable negotiating power despite the 15% minimum corporate tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Pillar Two has had broad-based consensus and therefore, jurisdiction after jurisdiction have been implementing their version of a domestic top-up tax, and we have too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But it does not change our broader assessment that even with the revenue upsides, we will have to spend more and we will have to find ways to strengthen our investment promotion toolkit, because notwithstanding the minimum corporate tax of 15%, which was supposed to give governments more negotiating power over the MNEs, the reality is MNEs still have considerable negotiating power.

sections.label: Revenue upside and competitive spending
sections.summary: The domestic top-up tax makes revenue upside more assured, but more spending on the economic front is likely to stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is the reality of the competitive landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the revenue upside is more assured, in terms of the domestic top-up tax, but at the same time, we are very likely to also have to spend more on the economic front to stay competitive.

sections.label: Rental caps not imposed
sections.summary: The situation remains stable overall, so rental caps are not envisaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There will always be a distribution of rental increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But overall, the situation remains stable, so we do not envisage imposing rental caps, particularly since at the macro level, the situation remains stable.

sections.label: Services dependency ratio ceiling
sections.summary: Services DRC is kept as a whole rather than carved out for F&B, though flexibilities may be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The DRC is lower than construction, but we prefer not to carve out something separate for F&B, because it is really very hard to distinguish between F&B as a service and the other service industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Once you make the DRC for F&B lower, you can be sure there will be many F&B foreign workers in Singapore doing non-F&B jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is very hard to enforce because they are all service-related.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we rather keep services DRC as a whole, where it is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But as I mentioned, where there are ways in which we can extend some flexibilities to businesses, like on the source of workers, we will consider doing so.

sections.label: Economic assumptions for fiscal projections
sections.summary: Economic assumptions underpinning fiscal projections will be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, yes, we will provide the economic assumptions underpinning our fiscal projections.

sections.label: Adaptation and rising sea levels
sections.summary: Resources are being set aside for adaptation work protecting Singapore against rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On adaptation, it is really about protecting Singapore against rising sea levels, and we will also find opportunities to share more about these plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have already started to set aside resources for these two areas of work, which will require a lot of additional investments, so we are already setting aside funds for that.

sections.label: Rental caps and supply shortages
sections.summary: Rental caps are not thought to work, though specific sharp rental increases may have particular causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We know that this happens, but the interventions and the way we help will have to take into account the different considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do not think rental caps will work, but for example, if we understand better a particular situation where there has been very sharp increase in rental for that location, it could be a supply source shortage, there could be specific circumstances linked to that area.

sections.label: Workers benefiting from growth
sections.summary: Additional levers and steps will be considered to ensure workers benefit from growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are, as I said in my speech, I did not highlight that in such terms, but that is the risk we are very much alive to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And if the trends in the marketplace globally are moving in that direction, well, we will have to consider what additional levers, what steps to take, how we ensure that workers benefit from growth.

sections.label: AI resources and opportunities
sections.summary: More resources will be allocated to pushing the AI frontier to expand opportunities, jobs and incomes for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: With AI and all the moves we talked about in AI, we will also allocate more resources to pushing the frontier, so that we can continually expand opportunities, jobs and better incomes for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Not only one-off measures
sections.summary: The approach does not rely only on one-off ad hoc measures, which make up 5% of the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because we do not rely only on one-off ad hoc measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have some, yes, 5% of the Budget.

sections.label: Resource allocation and reviews
sections.summary: 95% is allocated there, showing the emphasis, and reviews will be done from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: You can look at it from a resource issue: 95% allocated there; clearly, the emphasis is in these areas and the reviews will be done from time to time.

sections.label: Personal income tax suggestions
sections.summary: Mr Chua's personal income tax suggestions will be taken together with other Members' suggestions as part of regular fiscal reviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For the suggestions that Mr Chua had put forward on personal income tax, we will take them, as I had mentioned to Mr Saktiandi, together with other suggestions that Members have given as part of our regular fiscal reviews.

sections.label: Clean energy sources pursuit
sections.summary: New sources may not materialise short term, but work continues on importing clean energy, hydrogen and civilian nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The new sources may not materialise in the short term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are working on multiple fronts, including importing clean energy from outside Singapore, pursuing ideas like hydrogen, as well as civilian nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we are going full steam ahead on all of these areas so that we can find clean energy sources for ourselves that are reliable, sustainable, competitive, and that will help drive the industries of the future.

sections.label: Managing technology transition for workers
sections.summary: The transition to new technologies will be paced carefully, with retraining for workers if jobs are impacted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The assurance I gave then and I give now is that we will manage this very carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We already have very close engagement with the unions and drivers, and as we introduce these new technologies, we will pace the transition in a way that ensures that we are also able to retrain workers if jobs are impacted and make sure that the transition and the introduction of technologies do not adversely impact our workers.

sections.label: More funding for Government R&D
sections.summary: The speaker says that if results are good and good projects are secured, more will be put into Government R&D.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If we are getting good results, we are able to get good projects, certainly, we will be prepared to put more into Government R&D.

sections.label: Outcomes beyond company IPO success
sections.summary: The passage lists outcomes such as jobs created, spillovers to local industries and SMEs, wider economy and incomes, and business R&D expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is not just on the basis of a company getting IPO success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are outcomes with regard to jobs created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are outcomes with regard to the spillovers to local industries and the SMEs that support our MNEs doing research here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are outcomes to the wider economy and incomes that are raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are outcomes with regards to business expenditure on R&D, which we have talked about just now.

sections.label: Temasek's commercial mandate
sections.summary: Temasek was clear from the start that its mandate was commercial, not national service, focused on commercial outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Temasek, when it started, was always very clear about its mandate from the very beginning – commercial, not doing national service, focused on commercial outcomes.

sections.label: Strengthening social support system
sections.summary: The social support system has been progressively strengthened with Jobseeker Support and SkillsFuture, and AI's impact on vulnerable workers and seniors will be monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we have progressively strengthened our social support system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have put in place Jobseeker Support, we are strengthening SkillsFuture and we will continue to monitor this segment very closely and the impact that AI may have on vulnerable and disadvantaged workers, on seniors.

sections.label: Adoption, immigration and parenthood approach
sections.summary: The approach covers marriage, procreation and parenthood in Singapore, and also adoption and immigration, with adoption procedures to be reviewed for streamlining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Foo Cexiang gave a very good speech yesterday on adoption procedures and how it can be very complex and frustrating for parents who would like to adopt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think it is something that certainly we would want to take a closer look at to see how we can streamline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, our approach, as Minister Indranee will share during the COS, will not – of course, marriage, procreation, parenthood within Singapore is important, but also other areas, like adoption, as well as immigration will come in as well.

sections.label: Education agenda for disadvantaged groups
sections.summary: Education is a key agenda item this term, helping disadvantaged groups level up and addressing concerns about high-stakes exams and anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, many Members spoke about education during the debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I did not really touch on it as a topic in the round-up speech, but we have this as one of the key items on our agenda for this term of Government, looking at how we can especially help disadvantaged groups level up in our education system, focusing on those with less resources, those with different start points, making sure that more support is given to them, but at the same time addressing the other concern too, which many Members spoke about – the concerns about high-stakes exams, the anxiety about the arms race that parents and students are feeling.

sections.label: Maximising Singapore human potential
sections.summary: Singapore's long-term potential depends on maximising human potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, I would say the long-term potential of Singapore, how far we go really depends on us being able to maximise our human potential.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and social compact
sections.summary: Learning may need refreshing after graduation, so SkillsFuture is a key pillar of the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Whatever you have learned in school or from tertiary levels of education may very well need a refresh and an update a few years later after you graduate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is again why we are investing significantly in SkillsFuture and we have made it a key pillar in our social compact.

sections.label: Retirees and cost of living
sections.summary: Rising incomes guard against cost of living increases, but half a million retirees do not experience rising incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Specifically, he acknowledged that rising incomes are the best way to guard against increases in the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But he also acknowledged that for the half a million retirees in Singapore, they do not experience these rising incomes when the cost of living increases.

sections.label: Monitoring cost of living
sections.summary: The Government will continue to monitor cost of living across all segments of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To answer the question, we will continue to monitor cost of living across all segments of society.

sections.label: Support for mid-career PMETs
sections.summary: Schemes like Level-Up exist for those above 40, and the SSG-WSG merger may strengthen support for mid-career young seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I would like Prime Minister to share more about beyond merging WSG and SSG, and involving the IHLs and Institutes of Education (ITEs) more for continuing education and training, will the Government be looking at more measures to help our young seniors, especially the PMETs to stay effectively more relevant and more employable?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We know that at that mid-career level if you are made redundant, getting back into the workforce can be more challenging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Wage increases tend to be higher when you are younger and then, after a while, it starts to plateau off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we have already put in place schemes, like Level-Up for those above 40.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And we will continue to see how we can strengthen support for mid-career, young seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And with the merger of SSG and WSG, I am sure we can do more.

sections.label: Resources from good growth
sections.summary: Policies and schemes take time and resources, which Singapore has because its economy has done well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Policies take time, new schemes take resources and importantly, let us be very mindful, we are able to talk about all of these things and all the good things we can do because our economy has done well, because we have good growth and now, we are in a position with the resources to act decisively.
